bugs.summary: When credential sync is on (secret, key and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set) and the credential has a userId, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response, but the Google, HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Bigin callers treat the result as an axios/gaxios response or a token object, so the refresh fails or stores garbage.
bugs.evidence: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...); return response;` (return type any). The fallback returns whatever refreshFunction returns: googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:89 `return fetchTokens.res` then :94 `const token = res?.data;` :95 `token.access_token` -> TypeError on a Response (caught at :103, so the token silently never refreshes); hubspot CalendarService.ts:177 types the result as HubspotToken, :192 `expiresIn * 1000` -> NaN, :198 stores the Response as the key, :202 sets accessToken undefined; zohocrm :217 and zoho-bigin :96 `tokenInfo.data.error` -> TypeError. Fetch-based callers (office365 :262, zoom :96, lark :84, webex, office365video) handle a Response correctly, so the shape is inconsistent across callers. All callers are in the diff, hence reach diff. Golden comments (Martian cal_dot_com.json).

bugs.summary: Google refresh stores the safeParse wrapper ({success, data}) as the credential key, so on the next GoogleCalendarService construction googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws and the Google credential is unusable after its first refresh.
bugs.evidence: googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:97 `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and :100 `data: { key }`; parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 `return refreshTokenResponse;` (the safeParse result). The credential is read back unchanged at CalendarService.ts:75 `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (outside the diff), and googleCredentialSchema.ts requires top-level scope, token_type, expiry_date, access_token and refresh_token, none of which the wrapper has. Every other caller (office365 :263-264, zoom :104-111, salesforce) unwraps `.success`/`.data`. Golden comment.

bugs.summary: parseRefreshTokenResponse fills a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token", and callers merge it over the stored token, so a refresh response without a refresh_token (always the case on the sync path) destroys the real refresh token.
bugs.evidence: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. office365calendar CalendarService.ts:264 `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` then :270 stores it (refreshTokenResponseSchema :56 makes refresh_token optional); zoom VideoApiAdapter.ts:120 `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` then :124 stores it. On the sync path the minimum schema (:5-11) never keeps refresh_token, and refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7 says the endpoint returns only the access token and expiry. Golden comment.

bugs.summary: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which both evaluate to "[object Object]", so on the sync path the schema keeps only access_token and strips every other field: Zoom gets a NaN expiry_date, Office 365 keeps its old expires_in, and Salesforce (which refreshes directly but still parses through this helper) stores a key without instance_url.
bugs.evidence: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and :10 `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`: Zod schemas use Object.prototype.toString, so both keys are "[object Object]" and the later one wins; z.object strips undeclared keys by default, so expires_in/expiry_date are dropped. zoom VideoApiAdapter.ts:122 `Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` -> NaN; office365 CalendarService.ts:264 keeps the stale expires_in, so :279 isExpired stays true and every call refreshes. Re-anchored golden comment: it claims the schema throws at runtime, which it does not; the real defect is the collapsed key set. Salesforce: CalendarService.ts:90 parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema) takes the minimum-schema branch whenever sync is configured, :96-98 stores `{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token }`, and the next construction reads `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` (:105), now undefined. Findings that claim the sync schema 'always fails/rejects' valid responses match this entry's site but overstate it: the parse succeeds and strips.

bugs.summary: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id where refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com user id, so the sync endpoint is asked for another user's (or no) credentials.
bugs.evidence: zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:93 passes `credentialId` as the third argument; refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 `userId: number | null` and :11 `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`. CalendarService.ts:53 (outside the diff) `const credentialId = credential.id;`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`. Golden comment.

bugs.summary: Salesforce getClient now calls prisma.credential.update, but the file never imports prisma; @calcom/prisma only assigns globalThis.prisma when NODE_ENV !== "production", so in production every Salesforce client construction rejects with ReferenceError: prisma is not defined.
bugs.evidence: salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts imports (lines 1-20 at head) have no prisma import; :96 `await prisma.credential.update(...)`. It type-checks only because packages/prisma/index.ts declares `declare global { var prisma: ... }`, and that file sets `globalThis.prisma = prisma` only `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production")`. Upstream commit 833fe7c7b7 (#11839, 'don't declare prisma as a global object and explicitly import it') added `import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";` to exactly this file. Matches R2 v-no-speculation-medium ('prisma ... used without visible imports').

bugs.summary: Salesforce getClient now performs a blocking token refresh on every service construction and throws on any non-"OK" response, so a failing refresh request (which jsforce previously handled itself on 401) makes every Salesforce operation fail.
bugs.evidence: CalendarService.ts:75-84 unconditional fetch to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token, :86 `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`; this.conn = this.getClient(credential), so every method awaiting this.conn rejects. Before the PR getClient only built a jsforce.Connection with refreshToken, letting jsforce refresh on 401. Upstream fix 1d4eeab33e (#11508, 'fix: Salesforce by wrapping the refresh logic in a try/catch') wrapped the block in try/catch with the note 'This code results in Bad Request'. Likely rather than certain: the Bad Request cause is reported by upstream, not derivable from the code alone.
